chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Abbas ibn Amir from Yunus ibn Ya'qub said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who breastfed me and also breastfed a boy with me, and for that boy there is a brother from his father and mother; is it permissible for me to marry his daughter? He said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.أَخٌ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَأُمِّهِ: A brother from his father and mother (full sibling)
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the daughter of a boy who was breastfed by the same woman who breastfed him?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies a specific nuance in the rules of *radāʿ* (breastfeeding kinship), ruling that marriage is permissible when the nursing connection is established through a woman who breastfed both parties, provided the other party has full siblings, indicating the primary kinship link is clear. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the precise conditions under which breastfeeding creates a mahram relationship, distinguishing it from blood lineage. It serves as a practical legal precedent for determining marital eligibility in complex family structures involving wet-nursing.
